correctness.rationale: Componentwise proof checks all trees (including zero-edge components and small diameter) and cyclic components to give the sharp a_l/e bound. Under an unsuccessful history the conditional hit rate is exactly a_l/n. The path-template policy reaches the bound with expected O(1) wasted rounds up to O(sqrt(n)); summing hazard deficits yields uniform O(n^-1/2). Exhaustive graph tests through six vertices and explicit sharp witnesses corroborate but do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: First-cycle formation in the semi-random graph model is a central local-subgraph threshold observable. The theorem determines the entire first-hit distribution, sharp l-dependent coefficient, and an online optimal policy, substantially refining previously established scale-only results. The universal extremal exposure lemma is independently structural: it explains exactly why disjoint paths with 2l-3 edges are optimal templates for every fixed cycle length.
